[LUNI.4.6.2] **"The latest matching fact" means the greatest `asof`.**
When several live `FxRate` facts satisfy one `fx_pair` selector, the
conversion uses the one whose `asof` ([LUNI.13.3]) is greatest. Ties
on `asof` are a malformed feed: the conversion uses either, and an
implementation should surface the collision the same way it surfaces
the 1:1 fallback ([LUNI.4.6.1]).

Multiple live matches are the **normal** case, not an edge case:
`FxRate` is `scope ttl 1_h` ([LUNI.13.3]), and a `ttl` base
accumulates rather than upserting ([LSCP.2.5.7]), so a feed that
republishes hourly has several live facts per pair for most of the
hour.

`asof` is what the rest of the language already means by the word:
`latest` on a sequence anchor pins it to its **most recent match**
([LTHE.2.5.3]), lowered as a timestamp comparison ([LTHE.4.3]).
`FxRate` carries `asof` — "rate observation time" — for precisely this
purpose.

**This does not force a scan.** An implementation may keep a table
keyed by the selector tuple holding the greatest-`asof` entry seen,
updated on assert and retract; the requirement is only that `asof`
breaks the tie, not that arrival order does.
